scope: Proposition 7.4 (Compensated quadratic integration) of the manuscript “Marked polygon correlations and one-arc bounds” (preprints/Marked-polygon-correlations-and-one-arc-bounds-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 acb3276f993c6d8e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 47. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let F be real symmetric and bounded on X, with F ≥ gI, g > 0, and F − I trace class. Suppose its perturbation and a real linear functional h0(l, ·) are represented by smooth reflected physical kernels and tests. Let c ∈ R. For V (Q) = c + h0(l, Q) + 1 2h0(Q, (F − I)Q), mF = c − 1 2h0(l, F−1 l), one has log E0e−V (Q) ≤ −mF + C2L + 1 2 X λ<1, λ∈spec F − log λ. (44) The sum counts multiplicity. If the sharper source bound (43) holds, the gap is inverse-polynomial, and the data and required fixed-order derivatives have polynomial bounds, the same estimate on G has o(L) in place of C2L.
